status: fixture-qualified: a local and a remote agent read from one swarm view with backend, generation, pool class, observed state, wait kind and last seen time; a terminal view checked before the heartbeat is marked behind and never changes the card; reloading rebuilds the same cards from the store with no write; no Anton rollout of this commit has been observed
evidence_class: mocked: a fake Redis swarm store holds one published status for a mixed local and Kubernetes swarm and terminal views published after the heartbeat but checked before it; the swarm view the ledger server returns is read at a fixed clock; no ledger server, browser, worker Pod or cluster runs in these cases
interfaces: scripts.swarm.execution_card.card(agent, terminal) projects one published agent row and its terminal view into a card: agent, backend (runtime_backend, local when absent), generation, pool (the approved resource profile the Kubernetes adapter records on the agent profile field; empty for local), observed (the classification state, or the heartbeat value when unclassified, or unobserved), wait (scheduling for a pending state or pod_scheduling failure, quota for waiting_quota or provider_wait, input for an agent at an input prompt), seen_at (latest non terminal source time in ms) and terminal_behind (a terminal view checked strictly before the latest heartbeat)

scripts.swarm.execution_card.cards(agents, terminals) builds every card and counts ledger_state_projection_errors: a nameless row is skipped and counted; an unreadable row is counted and shown as observed unreadable with its backend, or unknown when it names none

scripts.swarm.commands.view(store, slug), which the ledger server returns from /api/swarm/<slug>, carries executions and ledger_state_projection_errors computed at read time from the stored status and terminal views; it writes nothing

The ledger Agents table adds an execution column before the terminal column whenever an agent runs off the local backend or a terminal view exists: the wait kind or observed state with its seen age on one line, and backend, generation and pool on a muted second line; the terminal cell appends behind heartbeat; a local only swarm keeps its nine column table, and the lane, state and master presentation is unchanged
authority: The card is a display projection: it grants nothing, and no control reads it. Execution identity and generation come from the swarm store, and the observation from the controller's classification; the page holds no client mutation for it.
authoritative_objects: The execution records, the observation classifications and the terminals hash stay authoritative. The cards are computed per read and stored nowhere; rollback deletes nothing.
rollback: Hide the new fields behind compatible response handling: without executions in the view, the page falls back to the existing nine or ten column table and every card keeps working. Rehearsed by the layout test of a local only swarm and the HDR-05 terminal test, which render without execution cards.
